solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Cup tie score upset Brussels fan? No!

indicators.note: something upset is knocked over and thrown into disorder, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A football reporter grumbles that a cup tie result has been overturned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' shuffles the letters of CUP TIE SCORE. The definition is a playful way of describing someone who says no to the European Union, based in Brussels.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone hostile to the European Union is certainly not a fan of its Brussels institutions.

clue.text: European vote result — only half rejoice

parts.note: a cross, X, is the mark made on a ballot paper

indicators.note: only half of the word result is kept here, its back three letters

explanation.surface: A referendum result in Europe leaves only half the voters celebrating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'only half' keeps the final three letters of 'result', ULT.
explanation.definitionFit: To exult is to be triumphantly happy, a close synonym of rejoicing.

clue.text: Being irritable, deserter, note on Scottish Loch

parts.note: a rat is someone who abandons a cause, like rats leaving a sinking ship
ti is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale
Loch Ness is the famous Scottish lake

explanation.surface: A deserter hiding out by a Scottish loch gets understandably irritable.
explanation.definitionFit: Ratty is informal British for bad-tempered, so the noun names the state of being peevish.

clue.text: Arrange extremely intense troop movement?

parts.note: to sort things is to arrange them in order

indicators.note: extremely asks for the extreme letters of the word intense, its first and last

explanation.surface: An order to organise a fierce manoeuvre of soldiers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremely' takes the outside letters of 'intense', I and E.
explanation.definitionFit: A sortie is a sally by troops out of a defended position, an example of a military movement, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Regularly tell off mischievous child

indicators.note: regularly asks for every other letter of the words tell off, starting with the second

explanation.surface: An instruction to scold a naughty youngster on a routine basis.
explanation.definitionFit: Elf is used affectionately for a small impish child, as well as the folklore sprite.

clue.text: 1960s satellite broadcast to inform celeb

indicators.note: something broadcast is spoken over the air, so the word is heard rather than written

parts.note: to tell someone is to inform them
a celebrity is a star

explanation.surface: A satellite used for broadcasting to keep a famous person informed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' gives TEL, which is pronounced like TELL.
explanation.definitionFit: Telstar, launched in 1962, was the first satellite to relay live television across the Atlantic.

clue.text: Bar, a nice base, served up American drink?

indicators.note: drinks served up at a bar are mixed, so these letters are mixed into a new order

explanation.surface: A cocktail bar with a nice setting serves an American beverage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'served up' shuffles the letters of BAR A NICE BASE. 'Drink' is slang for the sea, and this one lies off the Americas.
explanation.definitionFit: The drink is a jokey name for the sea, and this sea borders Central and South America.

clue.text: Manorial cost unfortunately very large

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests things have gone wrong, so the letters are thrown out of order

explanation.surface: The running costs of a manor house are, sadly, enormous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfortunately' rearranges the letters of MANORIAL COST.
explanation.definitionFit: Astronomical figures are as vast as the distances between stars, so it means huge.

clue.text: Relative in southeast river stroll

indicators.note: in places the relative within the compass abbreviation

parts.note: SE is the compass abbreviation for southeast
an aunt is a relative

explanation.surface: A family member takes a gentle walk by a river in the southeast of England.
explanation.definitionFit: To saunter is to walk in a slow, relaxed way, a synonym of stroll.

clue.text: Office clerk maybe initially fallible is later extremely reliable

indicators.note: initially asks for the opening letter of each of the five words that follow

explanation.surface: An office worker who makes mistakes at first becomes very dependable later on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremely' looks like an instruction for 'reliable' but is just one of the five words whose first letters are taken.
explanation.definitionFit: A filer is someone who files documents, one example of an office clerk's work, hence 'maybe'.

clue.text: Referring to pursuit: selling to customers

parts.note: re means about or with reference to, as in business letters
tailing someone is following or pursuing them

explanation.surface: A sales manual heading about the pursuit of customers.
explanation.definitionFit: Retailing is the business of selling goods directly to the public.

clue.text: Wine at finish in Kentish town

parts.note: Graves is a wine from the Bordeaux region of France
end means finish

explanation.surface: Drinking wine at the end of the night in a town in Kent.
explanation.definitionFit: Gravesend is a town on the Thames estuary in Kent, a county in southeast England.

clue.text: Brass instrument without a container

indicators.note: without means the a in the clue is left out

parts.note: the tuba is the largest brass instrument

explanation.surface: A brass instrument kept out of its case.
explanation.definitionFit: A tub is a round open vessel for holding things, a kind of container.

clue.text: Returning writer cut brother's son?

indicators.note: returning means the writing implement's letters are read backwards

parts.note: a pen is something that writes
to hew is to cut, as with an axe

explanation.surface: A writer comes back to edit a passage about a sibling's boy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Returning' turns PEN into NEP. The question mark is there because a sister's son would be one too.
explanation.definitionFit: A son of one's brother or sister is that person's nephew, so this is an example.

clue.text: Quietly including superfluous material

parts.note: p, for piano, is the musical direction for quietly
adding something means including it

explanation.surface: Quietly putting in unneeded extra stuff.
explanation.definitionFit: Padding is filler text or matter put in only to make something longer.

clue.text: Some minibar Riesling for Scottish dramatist

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A hotel guest takes some white wine from the minibar for a Scottish playwright.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft's definition included 'for', which is only a link word joining wordplay to definition; the definition proper is 'Scottish dramatist'.
explanation.definitionFit: J. M. Barrie, the Scottish playwright, wrote Peter Pan.

clue.text: Very formal at first — neckwear for sentimental guy

parts.note: so means very, as in so good

indicators.note: at first asks for the opening letter of the word formal

parts.note: a tie is worn around the neck

explanation.surface: A very formal man in a tie turns out to be a softy underneath.
explanation.definitionFit: A softie is a soft-hearted, easily moved person.

clue.text: Male editor's name for water

explanation.surface: A male editor names a body of water.
explanation.definitionFit: The Med is the familiar British short form for the Mediterranean, a name given to that stretch of sea.

clue.text: Anvil one's recycled — from the country

indicators.note: recycled material is broken down and remade, so these letters are reformed in a new order

explanation.surface: A blacksmith's old anvil is sent off to be recycled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recycled' rearranges the letters of ANVIL ONES. 'the country' means a particular nation, Slovenia, not countryside.
explanation.definitionFit: Slovenian describes something or someone coming from Slovenia, the country.

clue.text: Such entertainment: motoring

definitions.meaning: radio or music played to a driver and passengers on a journey
travelling by automobile means being inside one

explanation.surface: Entertainment of this kind keeps passengers amused on the road.
explanation.definitionFit: In-car entertainment is a common phrase, and while motoring one is sitting inside a vehicle.

clue.text: Cold atmosphere at new stone mound

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps
air is the atmosphere around us

explanation.surface: A chilly wind blows at a fresh pile of stones on a hilltop.
explanation.definitionFit: A cairn is a heap of stones raised as a landmark or memorial.

clue.text: Love Northern Ireland lake

parts.note: L is the map abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: Fondness for a lake in Northern Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Love' is a score of zero in tennis, not affection.
explanation.definitionFit: Love means zero in tennis scoring, the same as no score at all.

clue.text: Liquid needed for theatre — a clean-up

indicators.note: the letters needed are found inside the words theatre a clean-up

explanation.surface: Something wet is required for scrubbing down the theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: Treacle is a thick syrup, a sticky liquid made from sugar refining.

clue.text: Acceptable means of payment from cricket side — a lender absorbs it finally

parts.note: the leg side is the half of a cricket field behind the batter's legs

indicators.note: absorbs means takes something in, so one letter goes inside the words a lender

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: finally asks for the last letter of the word it

explanation.surface: A cricket team borrows money; the lender absorbs the cost in the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'absorbs' puts T, the last letter of 'it', inside A LENDER. In cricket the leg side is the half of the field behind a right-handed batter.
explanation.definitionFit: Currency that must by law be accepted in settling a debt is the official money of payment.
